notes: A handwritten English letter on a printed Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts 02138 / Department of Mathematics, 2 Divinity Avenue letterhead, dated Aug 4, 1969 and addressed Dear Grothendieck. The supplied H description attributes the letter to R. Hartshorne; the visible leaf has no signature. It quotes the title Exposé V. Systèmes projectifs J-adiques, par J.P. Jouanolou., asks which seminar the notes belong to and whether a later edition exists, and raises doubts about the proof of the Theorem of Shih, A.3.1, p.46. The writer says the p.45 lemma seems valid only for r>p, the equivalence of (i) and (ii) is not clear, and related doubts affect A.3.2, p.47 and Prop.5.3.1, p.40. He explicitly accepts the weaker parenthetical statement, suggests working in pro-A, asks whether the spectral sequence is biregular for finite filtration, and proposes n and n+1 in a hypothesis. These are the author’s statements, not mathematically verified conclusions. The page also contains a boxed pencil copying note, a left vertical pencil stroke, two cancellations and a tiny pair of right-side points. No own manuscript page number is visible; 53 is the archive number and appears only in a TeX comment. One scan leaf is read; the stated first-of-two status comes only from H and is not supplied as manuscript pagination. H is description-only, so every h_reading is null and every diff_h is false.
math_reading_decisions: Read the condition as r>p from the hooked and shouldered first letter, right-pointing strict angle, and descending p; no inequality is reversed.
Read the title numeral V and both lowered Roman III forms with separate upper and lower rules.
The leading EGA glyph remains 0/O ambiguous; mark the first occurrence with \unsure{0|O}, and use the first candidate at the repeated occurrence in accordance with the recurring-glyph convention.
The symbols pro-A and P_{AR} have plain single-stroke capitals; AR is a lower pair of capitals, not an exponent.
The first line indicator has a definite point above its minus, represented by \dot{-}1; the second is plain -1. This records the marks without assigning a mathematical function to the dot.

Retain each n, the crossing vertical stroke in n+1, and the horizontal-only stroke in n-1. All theorem/proposition numbers and the two EGA numerical citations were checked against their visible strokes.
No derivation, proof verification, computation, or appeal to the content of an external mathematical reference was performed.

completion: Complete independent page reading: the whole JPEG was viewed once for layout, then half a once and half b once in that order; ten remaining local places were cropped from the whole JPEG and each crop was viewed once. Every printed and handwritten text block, citation, mathematical letter/index/sign, visible cancellation, pencil note, frame, vertical grouping stroke and marginal point pair has been covered. Every explicit C doubt has a decision, including retained doubts; unmarked notation targets have also been reviewed without falsely classifying them as C doubts. H has no transcription. No other pages, peer readings, OCR, recognition software, web sources or TeX engines were used.
